---
title: "Setup & MCP Clients"
---

`measure-service` installs as a standard package with four CLI entrypoints (`measure-service`, `measure-service-client`, `measure-service-store`, and `measure-service-pilot`) and runs locally over **stdio** against a private SQLite store.

## 1. Install `measure-service`

From a checkout with Python 3.10+ (3.11+ if building docs locally):

```sh
python -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install .
```

On Windows, replace `.venv/bin/python` with `.venv\Scripts\python.exe`. For repeatable offline installations from exact source snapshots, see `docs/local-alpha-install.md` in the repository.

## 2. Install the analytical backends

Install `measure` and the corrected `measure.sec` backend into the R library visible to the service runtime so chromatogram processing, native acquisition validation, DAD/LC–MS inspection, and relative SEC are available:

```sh
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("remotes", "jsonlite", "tibble", "recipes"), repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'
Rscript -e 'options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org")); remotes::install_github("JamesHWade/measure@main", dependencies = NA)'
Rscript -e 'options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org")); remotes::install_github("JamesHWade/measure.sec@fix/separations-sec-correctness", dependencies = FALSE)'
Rscript -e 'for (p in c("measure", "measure.sec")) {d <- packageDescription(p); cat(p, d$Version, d$RemoteRef, d$RemoteSha, "\n")}'
```

::: {.callout-important title="Record installed backend revisions"}
Development version strings alone do not identify exact source code. Record the installed `RemoteSha` alongside analytical evidence, or pass `MEASURE_MCP_MEASURE_REVISION` and `MEASURE_MCP_SEC_REVISION` as operator declarations in the server environment.
:::

## 3. Generate MCP client settings

Use `measure-service-client config` to print safe, absolute-path client configuration fragments to stdout (it never mutates your existing configuration files):

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Claude Code (`.mcp.json`)

```sh
.venv/bin/measure-service-client config claude \
  --data-dir /absolute/path/to/private-measure-data \
  --r "$(command -v R)" \
  --r-library /absolute/path/to/R/library
```

Merge the printed JSON fragment into your project's `.mcp.json` and approve the server when prompted.

### Codex (`config.toml`)

```sh
.venv/bin/measure-service-client config codex \
  --data-dir /absolute/path/to/private-measure-data \
  --r "$(command -v R)" \
  --r-library /absolute/path/to/R/library
```

Merge the printed TOML block into `~/.codex/config.toml` or a trusted project's `.codex/config.toml`.

### Manual JSON (Cursor / Claude Desktop)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "measure": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/.venv/bin/python",
      "args": ["-m", "measure_service"],
      "env": {
        "MEASURE_MCP_DATA_DIR": "/absolute/path/to/private-measure-data",
        "MEASURE_MCP_R": "/usr/local/bin/R"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

:::

### Scoping tool groups and schema profiles

`measure-service` ships **82 tools across 12 groups**. To keep agent context lean, `measure-service-client config` defaults to `discovery`, `traces`, and `evidence` (add `--include-sec` to include SEC tools), or set `MEASURE_MCP_TOOL_GROUPS` to any JSON array of group names (`discovery`, `traces`, `sec`, `dad`, `ms`, `evidence`, `batches`, `methods`, `experiments`, `observations`, `retention`, `campaigns`). Passing `--schema-profile canonical` retains full canonical JSON schemas instead of the compact `function-host/1` projection.

## 4. Verify your installation

Run the built-in stdio verification command in an isolated temporary store before connecting real data:

```sh
.venv/bin/measure-service-client check
```

To also verify the full analytical trace and relative SEC backends end-to-end across a process restart:

```sh
.venv/bin/measure-service-client check \
  --include-sec \
  --numerical \
  --r "$(command -v R)" \
  --r-library /absolute/path/to/R/library
```

You can also run the standalone workflow scripts directly from the checkout:

```sh
.venv/bin/python examples/registry.py
.venv/bin/python examples/methods.py
MEASURE_MCP_R="$(command -v R)" .venv/bin/python examples/analyze_trace.py
```

## Common setup failures

| Failure | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| `measure_service` cannot be imported | Ensure your MCP client invokes the exact virtual environment where `measure-service` is installed. |
| Analytical worker fails to start or times out | Verify `MEASURE_MCP_R` points to `R` (not `Rscript`), pass `--r-library` when using a non-default library, and confirm calls finish within the 90-second worker limit. |
| SEC reports missing calibrated-curve support | Install the corrected `measure.sec` branch (`fix/separations-sec-correctness` until merged). |
| Tool returns unexpected `isError` | Check `MEASURE_MCP_TOOL_GROUPS` to confirm the tool's group is enabled in your client config. |
| Idempotency key conflict | Reuse the exact original request arguments for retries, or supply a fresh `idempotency_key` for a new operation. |
